title: update moves the SeamSpec pin forward only, and every workflow and .swerepo.toml name the same version
assertion: In a repository set up by `swerepo init` with SeamSpec set up and chosen, the CI pinning SeamSpec 0.1.2, and a fake `seamspec` first on PATH reporting its version: `swerepo update --yes --only seamspec` with 0.2.0 installed moves the pin to 0.2.0 in `.swerepo.toml`'s `[tools] seamspec` and `swerepo-ci.yml` (`ci` brought along for the pin), and in strict mode in SWERepo's `seamspec.yml` too. With 0.1.1, 0.1.2, a development build (0.3.0.dev0) or a local build (0.3.0+local) installed, `swerepo-ci.yml`, `seamspec.yml` and `.swerepo.toml` stay byte for byte. When the person edited the `seamspec==` line in `swerepo-ci.yml`, `update --yes --merge --only seamspec` with 0.2.0 installed leaves all three byte for byte. In strict mode, a person's edit to `seamspec.yml` (so `update --yes` without `--merge` can't take the new pin there) leaves all three byte for byte. After every run, each of these workflows pins SeamSpec, and all of them and `[tools] seamspec` name the same version.

origin.text: ADR-20261124-cd64 point 8 and the owner's watchout 4 (2026-11-24): -u --seamspec moves the pin to the installed version, never backwards and never to a development build, with ci brought along for the pin only; the pin and the workflows move together or not at all. The strict-mode hold from Gemini's Phase 7 review (P7-F01); tightened twice after SeamSpec's reviewer: the fake on PATH, the strict-mode upgrade, whole files compared byte for byte, a pin required in each workflow, and a local build.
